Multi-penalty permutation selection of edges

Source: R/ridgegraph.R
mps_select.Rd

Selects the pairs whose ridge partial correlation exceeds a permutation threshold at some penalty in a grid. For each penalty the threshold is an order statistic of the maximal absolute partial correlation over the observed data and B data sets in which each column is permuted independently, at level alpha divided by the number of penalties.

Usage

mps_select(x, mult = c(0.3, 1, 3, 10), B = 99L, alpha = 0.1)

Arguments

x

numeric data matrix with observations in rows.

mult

penalty grid in units of \(\mathrm{tr}(S) / p\).

B

number of permutations.

alpha

level in \((0, 1)\).

Value

A list with the logical adjacency matrix, the penalties lambda and the thresholds threshold.

Details

If the rows of x are independent and identically distributed and its columns are mutually independent, the probability that any edge is selected is at most alpha, for every sample size and dimension. No edge can be selected unless B + 1 >= length(mult) / alpha.

References

Arashi, M. and Ebrahim, E. K. (2026). What does a ridge network estimate? Effective penalty and leakage in ridge precision matrix estimation. Submitted.

Examples

set.seed(1)
x <- matrix(rnorm(60 * 8), 60, 8)
x[, 2] <- x[, 1] + rnorm(60, sd = 0.5)
sel <- mps_select(x, B = 49)
which(sel$adjacency & upper.tri(sel$adjacency), arr.ind = TRUE)
#>      row col
#> [1,]   1   2
